Dear Author,

I am reaching out to discuss my difficulty understanding the results obtained from the msstatsTMT package. Specifically, we ran the groupComparisonTMT function using the compare_analysis = groupComparisonTMT(data = processed_data, contrast.matrix = comparison, moderated = TRUE) command and exported the results to a CSV file using write.csv(compare_analysis$ComparisonResult, "comparison1.csv").

Upon reviewing the output file, we observed two issues. Firstly, when we examined the top proteins in the "processed_data$ProteinLevelData" data, we found that the direction of log2FC values was inconsistent for multiple proteins. Additionally, we attempted to calculate the t-test and log2FC values manually, but the results were not consistent with those generated by msstatsTMT. We would appreciate any insights into how the log2FC values are calculated and how we can better understand the results.

As a potential solution, we attempted to calculate the log2FC values using the following Python code, adjusting for the number of samples based on the plexing used:

import pandas as pd
import numpy as np
from scipy.stats import ttest_ind

def log2_fold_change(x, y):
    return np.log2((np.mean(x) + 1e-8) / (np.mean(y) + 1e-8)) ##added a small value 1e-8 so that if denominator is zero we still have some value that will allow to run the function normally

data = pd.read_csv("btvssst_processprotein.csv", skipinitialspace=True)

data['Abundance'] = data['Abundance'].astype(float)

results = pd.DataFrame(columns=["Protein", "Label", "log2FC", "t-statistic", "p-value", "adj.p-value"]) ##output we needed in the csv file

total_samples_BT = 13
total_samples_SST = 16

for protein in data["Protein"].unique():
    protein_data = data[data["Protein"] == protein]

    bt_values = protein_data[protein_data["Condition"] == "BT"]["Abundance"]
    sst_values = protein_data[protein_data["Condition"] == "SST"]["Abundance"]

    if len(bt_values) == 0 or len(sst_values) == 0:  # ADDED condition to remove any protein present if only in one condition
        continue

    bt_values = np.append(BT_values, [0] * (total_samples_BT - len(ssm_values)))
    sst_values = np.append(sst_values, [0] * (total_samples_SST - lenbt_values)))

    t_statistic, p_value = ttest_ind(bt_values, sst_values, equal_var=False)
    log2fc = log2_fold_change(bt_values, sst_values)

    results = results.append({
        "Protein": protein,
        "Label": "BTvsSST",
        "log2FC": log2fc,
        "t-statistic": t_statistic,  # Added t-statistic to the results DataFrame
        "p-value": p_value,
        "adj.p-value": None
    }, ignore_index=True)

results["adj.p-value"] = results["p-value"] * len(results) / (np.arange(len(results)) + 1)

results.to_csv("t_test_results_bt-sst.csv", index=False)

However, even with this approach, we still observed inconsistencies with the results generated by msstatsTMT.

We would greatly appreciate any assistance you can provide in better understanding these results and determining potential solutions to these issues.

Thank you for your time and attention.

Best regards,

Devender

Dear MSstats team,

we would love to test the advance methods in MSstats for feature selection and outlier filtering in our large patient cohorts measured in DIA.

We use DIA-NN in our searches.

I wanted to comment in this thread because I have noticed that the DIANNtoMSstats converter is not working.

I have debugged the function and believe to have found the culprit.

It seems the cleanDIANN function is removing everything with an NA from the final DIANN table.

see line 37 in clean_DIANN function <https://github.com/Vitek-Lab/MSstatsConvert/blob/master/R/clean_DIANN.R> .

I re-wrote the functions locally with this modification and now I get the expected result, based on a DIANN output from ours, version 1.8.

Sadly I can't promise I would make a pull request in GitHub to collaborate with this modification, because I am short in time.

Best wishes,
Miguel

messages.body_plain:
Dear MSstats-developers,

I performed an phosphoproteomic experiment with 4 treatments in 4 biological replicates each (=total 16 samples). From each sample I have the total sample (=proteome) and two phosphoenriched fractions (TiO2, FeNTA). The separate phospho fractions were actually generated by tandem-enrichment following Thermo's SMOAC-protocol, meaning that the flow trough of TiO2 was again run over a Fe-NTA-column.
I now ran the samples trough Spectronaut in two separate searches, once only the total total 16 proteome samples, and once the 32 phosphosamples. In the later search I labeled the individual phosphofractions in Spectronaut with unique identifiers during the experimental setup (TiO2, FeNTA).
My question now is, if this is a sensible setup for MSstats-PTM to handle? Because of the two phospho fractions, the current long Spectronaut report will have quite some rows matching to exactly the same phosphopeptide but coming from different fractions. I assume MSStats by default will use only the most intense feature for a peptide according to the summaryforMultipleRows parameter? Since the actual amount of t such a peptide is actually the sum of its intensity in both fractions I guess I should rather use the "sum"-option for this parameter?
Or is MSStats treating fractions in a special way?

Best and thanks for this awesome piece of software.

Robert

Hi Robert,

>From your description it sounds like this is a DIA dataset with a lot of features per protein and the steps you took above were definitely the way to go.

The reason the protein dataset is taking longer is most likely due to the number of features per protein being very high. We do not usually run into this issue with the PTM dataset because we have a much lower feature count (e.g. the features have to span the same modification site).

In these cases, we recommend doing what you did and reducing the number of features. You should not see major analysis differences, and it will greatly decrease your processing time.

Additionally, in terms of the "Warning: Ran out of iterations and did not convergeWarning: Ran out of iterations and did not converge" message, I would not worry about this. This was caused by the summarization for a PTM not converging, most likely due to only having one (or two) features. As long as the summarized values make sense for your PTMs you should be good to go.

I think your analysis should work well with what you described above but definitely get back in touch if you continue to see problems.

Devon

Yes this is the intended behavior. We summarize all peptides spanning the same modification site together (not including peptides with multiple modifications, which are summarized separately). input$ProteinName = paste(input$ProteinName,  input$PeptideSequence, sep="_")

messages.subject: How to interpret lower protein quantitation when imputation is turned off?
messages.subject_clean: How to interpret lower protein quantitation when imputation is turned off?
messages.body_plain:
Hello again to the MSstats team.

I am trying to understand how MSstats' imputation model affects protein quantitation. I found Devon's explanation for how imputation works during the summarization step <https://groups.google.com/g/msstats/c/aBm8sEWT1BA/m/3kVemCNBBQAJ>, and I was trying to understand what happens when I turn imputation on/off. I wonder if you could clarify why some of the quantitation in the data increases / decreases based on imputation.

Imputation is recommended to be turned on most of the time, and so the default function call is:

MSstats::dataProcess(
  msstats_data,
  censoredInt = "NA",
  MBimpute = TRUE
)

I am not sure I understand 100% how "censoredInt" changes the treatment of values in imputation, but I think the option means that only "NA" values are treated as candidates for possible imputation. "MBimpute" of course means that data is imputed.

Following the MSstats user manual <https://msstats.org/msstats-2/msstats_v4-6-3_manual-1/> section 4.1.4, I can disable imputation by changing two options:

MSstats::dataProcess(
  msstats_data,
  censoredInt = NULL,
  MBimpute = FALSE
)

where "censoredInt = NULL" tells MSstats that data is missing at random (and therefore not suitable for imputation by the accelerated failure model), and disables imputation.

I compared the protein-level quantitation with imputation enabled / disabled, and I observed:
about half of my data has their quantitation affected
of the data affected, about 1/4 of the data has increased in quantitation with imputation off and censoredInt=NULL
the other 3/4 of the affected data has decreased in quantitation.
Could you help explain to me what has changed in MSstats treatment of the data to cause the increase / decrease in protein-level quantitation?

I can possibly explain why some proteins would have increased quantitation with imputation turned off. When MSstats imputes on missing values near the limit of quantification, these low values "drag down" the summarized value of the protein in that sample. Is my understanding on this point correct?

However, I can't explain why many proteins have actually decreased in quantitation when imputation is turned off. My best guess is that, when "MBimpute=TRUE," the imputed fragments are added to the overall intensity of that protein, so disabling imputation removes these fragments from the equation. However, this does not make sense to me based on how Devon has explained imputation in the previous post.

I would appreciate any insights you could give on this topic.

Many thanks,
Jonathan
